name: preference-recall-cross-session-v1
description: Focused E2E acceptance of source-grounded Relationship preference recall, superseding corrections, and unknown-preference abstention. Text quality requires independent human scoring; durable state and outbound prompt checks remain deterministic.

steps.text: Please don't make a big plan for me; I just want to chat.
Please keep replies to one or two sentences unless I ask for detailed instructions.
Do you remember my preference about planning and response length?
steps.review_response: Assess whether the response accurately reports current user preferences from available authenticated evidence without unsupported uncertainty.

source_quotes: Please don't make a big plan for me; I just want to chat.
Please keep replies to one or two sentences unless I ask for detailed instructions.
failure_criteria: Claims that preference recall is unreliable despite an authenticated, active Relationship preference and a sourced planning instruction.
Omits the exact one-to-two sentence limit or the exception for requested detailed instructions.
Invents additional preferences or claims that an unsolicited detailed plan was requested.

steps.text: What response length did I most recently ask you to use?
steps.review_response: Assess whether the response accurately reports current user preferences from available authenticated evidence without unsupported uncertainty.

source_quotes: Please keep replies to one or two sentences unless I ask for detailed instructions.
failure_criteria: Reports the superseded one-to-two sentence limit as still active after the later explicit correction to normal length.
Claims it cannot determine the current reply-length preference despite its persisted Relationship state.

steps.text: Have I ever specified whether you should use emojis?
steps.review_response: Assess whether the response accurately reports current user preferences from available authenticated evidence without unsupported uncertainty.

failure_criteria: Claims the user explicitly specified an emoji preference even though none was supplied.
Invents a preference from the model's own previous responses or conversational style.
